prompt:
You are a grounded brand-outreach assistant for our team. Use only the evidence passages below.
Never use outside knowledge. Return valid JSON only.

Separate three things:
1. OBSERVED FACTS - things a passage actually states about this company. Each fact is a claim with an id (C1, C2, ...),
   the passage id(s) that support it, and an exact quote copied word-for-word from that passage.
2. UNKNOWNS - things the evidence does not tell us (put them in "unknowns"). A channel, program or audience that does
   not appear in these passages is UNKNOWN. It is never a weakness, never a "gap", and never a reason for outreach.
3. PROPOSALS - collaboration ideas from our team. Proposals are not facts, but each must build on a positively supported
   fact (an existing campaign, partnership, product, community, value or theme) and cite that premise.

Rules:
- Put a claim marker like {C1} (curly braces) right after every factual statement in every field, including the
  email and Instagram idea. Do not write citation numbers yourself; markers are converted to citations later.
- A claim's "quote" must be copied character-for-character from the cited passage: 5 to 25 consecutive words, no
  paraphrasing, no joining of separate sentences. If you cannot find such a quote, drop the claim and every sentence
  that depends on it.
- Audience and strategy sentences are factual: each needs a marker. If no passage states the audience, write
  INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of guessing.
- Pitch lines (email subject, hook, concept) should describe the proposed post ("A carousel featuring ...",
  "Collaborate on ..."). Any statement in them about what the company already does needs a marker.
- Respect passage types. "proposed_or_mock_work" and "author_recommendation" passages describe ideas, not things the
  company did: never state them as company activity. "provider_reported_result" passages are claims by a vendor or
  agency: attribute them ("X reports that ..."). "creator_or_influencer_audience_data" describes creators' followers,
  not the company's customers. "vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics" passages are a tool vendor's estimates
  (e.g. inferred age ranges): attribute them and never present them as the company's own data.
  "forward_looking_statement" passages describe plans or intentions, not completed activity.
- Mind time: if a passage describes past activity, do not present it as current.
- "marketing_gaps" may only contain a weakness that a passage positively states. Usually it is [].
- Never promise results. Describe benefits as goals or possibilities ("could", "aims to"), not guaranteed outcomes.
- Decision: write "draft" when at least one concrete, evidence-supported collaboration opportunity exists. Otherwise write
  "abstain", give an abstain_reason, set pitch fields to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and leave collaboration_opportunities empty.
- The email is from our team to the company, proposing one collaborative Instagram post. The pitch, the post idea and
  every collaboration opportunity are for Instagram only (no TikTok, YouTube, podcasts or other channels).
- When a sentence uses a vendor, agency or analytics passage, name that source in the sentence itself
  ("According to AdLibrary, ...", "Attentive reports that ...").
- Each "unknowns" item names one specific thing the passages do not tell us (e.g. "Whether X runs a creator program").
  Never write placeholder text such as "what the evidence does not show".

Required JSON:
{
  "decision": "draft" or "abstain",
  "abstain_reason": "string or empty",
  "claims": [{"id": "C1", "kind": "fact | provider_reported | premise", "statement": "string",
              "passage_ids": ["P1"], "quote": "exact words from the passage"}],
  "brand_summary": "Full sentences, each followed by its marker, e.g. "X makes ... {C1}." Never only markers. Or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "likely_target_audience": "A full sentence followed by its marker, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "current_marketing_strategy": ["text with markers"],
  "unknowns": ["one specific open question, e.g. Whether the company works with creators"],
  "marketing_gaps": [],
  "collaboration_opportunities": ["proposal that builds on a cited fact {C2}"],
  "instagram_post_idea": {"hook": "string", "concept": "string", "why_it_fits": "string"},
  "email_subject": "string",
  "email_body": "string"
}

Company: Tatcha (company_id tatcha; category: Japanese-inspired skincare)
Official domains: tatcha.com
Recipient: the marketing team
Packet status: ok

Evidence passages:
[P1] source: https://tatcha.com/pages/our-story | document: official_domain | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Skin and Mind Are One Tatcha began with a simple truth discovered in Japan: that caring for the skin is also a way of caring for the mind. Zen monk Toryo Ito introduced Vicky to the Japanese phrase hinou-dokon (皮脳同根), meaning \"skin and mind, same root\"—a reminder that our inner and outer selves are deeply connected, each shaping and reflecting the other. It became one of the ideas at the heart of Tatcha, inspiring our commitment to NeuroSkin Science and the work of the Tatcha Institute in Tokyo."

[P2] source: https://tatcha.com/pages/our-story | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Founding Team Tatcha was not built by one person. It was built by a team whose expertise, knowledge, and care shaped everything from the science to the soul of the brand."

[P3] source: https://beautero.com/articles/tatcha-target-comprehensive-overview/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Influencer Collaborations and Marketing In today’s digital age, strategic collaborations with influencers can make or break a luxury brand’s visibility. Tatcha has adeptly utilized this avenue by partnering with beauty influencers and content creators who resonate with their target market. Such collaborations have helped amplify Tatcha's message while lending authenticity to its promotional efforts. Influencers often provide a personal touch that large advertising campaigns may lack. The reviews and demonstrations shared by these influencers resonate with their followers, creating a sense of trust and relatability."

[P4] source: https://beautero.com/articles/tatcha-target-comprehensive-overview/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"This direct connection engages the audience differently than traditional marketing methods. Furthermore, Tatcha’s marketing strategy involves creating exclusive engagement opportunities for both influencers and consumers. Events that allow for an immersive brand experience can foster deeper connections. By leveraging influencer networks, Tatcha can reach niche audiences effectively, enhancing its brand positioning as a leader in luxury skincare. Tatcha's careful curation of partnerships ensures that the brand remains aligned with individuals who reflect its values, thus maintaining the integrity of its luxury image while expanding its reach in a crowded market."

[P5] source: https://beautero.com/articles/tatcha-target-comprehensive-overview/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Social Media Presence Tatcha's social media presence is a vital component of its digital marketing strategy. Platforms like Instagram and Facebook serve as visual stages where the brand showcases its luxurious offerings. The curated aesthetic of the Tatcha profile attracts users who appreciate high-quality images and sophisticated branding. Such visual appeal aligns with the expectations of luxury consumers, who often seek not just a product but a complete experience. Engagement on these platforms goes beyond mere advertising. Tatcha often employs user-generated content, showcasing real customers using their products."

[P6] source: https://tatcha.com/pages/our-story | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Impact Tatcha’s commitment to education and opportunity comes to life through a deep partnership with Room to Read, a global organization that supports girls' literacy around the world and helps build confidence for the next generation."

[P7] source: https://tatchacosmetics.com/about-us/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: brand_positioning | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"We believe skincare should feel like a moment of calm, a daily ritual that honors both your skin and your spirit.Beyond creating beautiful products, we’re committed to doing beautiful things. Through our partnership with Room to Read, we’ve helped millions of girls access education across Asia and Africa, because we believe true beauty begins with opportunity and empowerment.Welcome to Tatcha. Where every bottle holds a story, every routine becomes a ritual, and radiant skin is just the beginning."

[P8] source: https://adlibrary.com/brands/tatcha-instagram-ads | document: third_party_confirmed | type: provider_reported_result | flags: vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics | dates in text: 2009, 2019 | published: unknown
"About Tatcha Tatcha is a San Francisco-based luxury skincare brand founded in 2009 by Victoria Tsai, inspired by Japanese geisha beauty rituals. Acquired by Unilever in 2019 for ~$500M, it remains a top seller at Sephora with the Dewy Skin Cream as its flagship."
